findings.title: VIEW permission on all groups grants manage access
findings.body: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() calls hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE). This means that a caller with only the VIEW scope on all groups will be considered as having manage permission. As a result, any operation requiring requireManage(), such as creating groups, adding child groups, or updating groups, will be allowed without the MANAGE scope. The method should only check the MANAGE scope. This is a privilege escalation vulnerability.

findings.title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission returns resource IDs instead of group IDs
findings.body: In the callback of resourceStore.findByType, the method adds groupResource.getId() to the granted set. Resource.getId() is the internal authorization resource UUID, which is not the same as the group ID. The returned set is later used in UsersResource.searchForUser and getUsersCount to filter users by group membership via session.setAttribute(UserModel.GROUPS, groupIds). Since the IDs are wrong, the filtering will not match any group, causing legitimate users to be hidden or search results to be empty. The method should instead use groupResource.getName(), which contains the group ID.

findings.title: Individual group resources are not assigned the Groups resource type
findings.body: When getOrCreateResource creates a new resource for a specific group (resourceType = GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE), it does not call resource.setType(GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE) after creation. Later, GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission uses resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...) to discover group resources. Because the resources lack the type, they will not be returned, causing group-scoped view-members permissions to be ignored during user search and count queries. This breaks the ability to see users based on group VIEW_MEMBERS or MANAGE_MEMBERS permissions.

findings.title: Missing fallback to all-groups permission when a specific group resource exists
findings.body: In hasPermission, if a specific group resource exists (resource != null), the method evaluates only that resource's permissions. It does not fall back to the all-groups resource when the specific resource has no policy granting the requested scopes. Consequently, once a group-specific resource is created (e.g., via a single permission like MANAGE), a user with an all-groups VIEW or MANAGE permission may be denied access to that group for other scopes, because the all-groups policy is not considered. The fallback should occur not only when the resource is null, but also when the evaluation against the specific resource yields no matching permission.
